gloss.intro: The words developers (and the AI teams) use, in plain English.
gloss.switch.help: An explanation, dotted words get when you hover them.
gloss.backlog.text: Ideas and work not planned in yet. Worked on, nothing there is, until to To do it moves.
gloss.sprint.text: A short stretch of work (often a week or two), with an agreed set of cards to finish.
gloss.standup.text: A quick check-in: what each team member did, what they do next, and what is stopping them.
gloss.bug.text: The way it should, something that doesn’t work.
gloss.test.text: A finished piece of work, trying it is, to check it does what was asked, before you accept it.
gloss.commit.text: A saved snapshot of the code, with a short note of what changed. Go back to one, you always can.
gloss.push.text: Saved snapshots (commits) from this computer up to GitHub, sending them is, so backed up and shared they are.
gloss.branch.text: A separate line of work in the code, so changes made can be without touching the main version.
gloss.merge.text: Into the main version, a branch’s changes joining back.
gloss.repo.text: The project’s folder of code and its full history of commits, usually on GitHub also kept.
gloss.refactor.text: The code, tidying, without changing what it does: smaller files, clearer names, less repetition.
gloss.deploy.text: Live, a new version putting, for example onto a server where people use it.
gloss.kanban.text: A board with columns (To do, In progress, Done), where left to right cards move as work happens.
gloss.wip.text: Work in progress: the most cards a column should hold, so things finished the team does, before more it starts.
gloss.pr.text: Checked and merged into the main version, a branch’s changes to be, asking for that this is.
gloss.hook.text: A small command that runs by itself at a set moment, e.g. when an AI session starts, so your comments the team hears.
gloss.token.text: The unit AI usage is counted in: roughly a few letters of text read or written. Fewer tokens, more of your plan left.
gloss.agent.text: An AI that works on its own on a task: the code it reads, changes it makes, checks it runs, and back it reports.

gloss.title: 📖 Words explained, these are
gloss.about: The words you meet in AI-gile, in plain language they are: building it, changing it safely, running it keeping for the people who use it, and as a team with AI working.
gloss.about.noai: The words you meet in AI-gile, in plain language they are: building it, changing it safely, running it keeping for the people who use it, and as a team working.
gloss.g.team: 🤝 As a team working (and with AI)
gloss.qa.text: Short for quality assurance, it is: the automatic checks that run before live anything goes. When red QA is, failed something has, and live it cannot go until fixed that is.
gloss.release.text: A named bundle of finished work, together live it goes, with short notes on what changed. From the done cards, 🚀 Releases writes the notes.
gloss.rollback.text: When trouble a new version causes, back to the last version that worked you go. In AI-gile, a checklist of the undo steps written on each change, it makes.
gloss.live.text: The real version that people use, this is, not a copy for things trying out. Production, developers also call it.
gloss.change.text: A planned change to something people rely on, first written down: what, why, the risk, when, and how to undo it. With 🔀 Raise a change, one start you do.
gloss.risk.text: Something that wrong could go, scored on how likely and how bad it would be. In one list, ⚠️ Risks keeps them, highest score first, each with a date to look again.
gloss.chgwin.text: The times when live changes may go, such as a quiet Tuesday evening. Outside a window, finished a change card cannot be, unless an emergency it is.
gloss.gonogo.text: A quick vote, just before live a change goes: Go or No go, each person who must approve says. Only when they agree, ahead it goes.
gloss.approval.text: For a yes waiting, before work starts. A card a friend raises, or a change, in ✅ Approvals it waits, until approve or decline it you do.
gloss.quiettime.text: A stretch of time, like a stream, a demo or the night, when live nothing goes. Working and testing, the teams keep, but until it ends, going live waits. A change freeze, elsewhere it is called.
gloss.service.text: Something you built that people rely on, like a website or an app, looked after so working it keeps. Tick “A service, this project is”, and say what it offers, who uses it and who on call is.
gloss.uptime.text: An automatic check, every few minutes, that still your service answers. If several times in a row it fails, an incident card by itself AI-gile opens.
gloss.statuspage.text: A public page, whether working a service is it shows (green, orange or red), with the latest update, so check instead of ask, the people who use it can.
gloss.incident.text: Broken for the people using it right now, something is, like the website down being. The queue, a 🔥 incident card jumps: working again getting it, first comes.
gloss.major.text: A big incident, this is: many people affected, or at risk money or data are. Every team on it, one button puts (swarm), whoever on call is it wakes, and a status update every 30 minutes it asks for.
gloss.oncall.text: The one who answers when something breaks, even at night, being. An on-call team member, each service has; first woken for its incidents, they are.
gloss.replyby.text: How long for a first answer a card may wait, for example an hour for an incident. After that, a red clock it gets, so quietly forgotten nothing is. A response target, also called it is.
gloss.postmortem.text: A short look back after an incident: what happened, what helped and what to change, blaming no one. Without one, closed an incident cannot be.
gloss.problem.text: The hidden cause behind one or more incidents, it is. Incidents that keep coming back, a 🧩 problem card groups, so found and fixed for good the cause is.
gloss.rootcause.text: The real reason something broke, not just what going wrong you saw. Fix the root cause, and coming back the incident stops.
gloss.workaround.text: A way to keep things working until ready the real fix is, like something restarting when stuck it gets. On the problem card written it is, so work it out again nobody has to.

- **Service details:** in **🎨 Look**, **Project settings**, **🛎️ Service**, what a project offers, to whom, at what web address and who on call is, you say. Only projects you tick, as services count.
- **Uptime dot:** every few minutes, the web address if alive it is, the board asks. Green, fine is; red means answer it did not. Three misses in a row open one incident, never a pile, and when back it was, a comment says ("Up again after N min").
- **Reply-by ⏰:** a time to reply by, each kind of card has (an incident about an hour, a friend request a couple of days, a bug about a week). Red, late cards go, and them the daily brief lists. Aims these are, not promises.
- **🚨 Major:** for an incident that many users hurts, or money or data risks. One click the swarm turns on, the on-call agent wakes, you one note sends, and every 30 minutes for a "Status:" comment asks.
- **Status page:** each public service as green, orange or red with the latest status line, a public page shows. Card text it never shows, only the line you or the agent chose.
- **Service desk:** into **Request**, **Incident** or **Idea**, reports from friends and the feedback form are sorted. One kind, the inbox filter shows (**Desk: all**, **Desk: requests** and so on). "Looks like AIG-12" with a **Link** button, a report that looks like a card you already have says.
- **🧩 Known errors:** a problem with a known cause and a workaround, not done yet. Per project and for all projects listed they are, and into each agent's brief they go, so twice, nobody investigates.
- **📖 Runbooks:** short step-by-step notes on how to fix a thing. The ones that match its title, an incident card shows. After a review, a new runbook the agent can propose, and Go or Not yet you say.
- **📝 Post-incident review:** after done a major incident is, a **Timeline**, **What helped** and **What to change** the agent writes. A card, each action becomes with **Make a card**. If free no agent is, yourself you write it.
- **🗂️ Items:** the list of things a service stands on, with a **Kind** (server, domain, certificate, key, repo, supplier, other). Links to cards or web addresses, each can have. Only its name from Secrets, a key is, never the key itself. What they **Affect**, incident and change cards can show.
- **Expiry and backups:** each day, expiry dates and backup age the board checks. Before something runs out or when too old a backup is, a card appears, and once a month a restore-test card reminds you: only a hope, a backup you never tried to restore is.
- **Server health:** CPU, memory and disk on your servers, the board watches, and before they fill up, an upgrade card it raises.
- **🔐 Access review:** every 90 days, share links, friends' roles and kept secrets (names only) one card lists, each with **Keep** or **Remove**. From **Setup**, now run it.
- **🚀 Releases:** a named bundle of the cards that done became since the last one, with short notes, a release is. A checklist card with the undo steps, **↩ Roll back** files.
- **📈 Improvements:** retro suggestions, review actions and problem fixes in one list, filterable by project, so lost between retros, good ideas do not get.
- **📆 Monthly review:** one page per service for one month: incidents opened and closed, average time to fix, cards that their reply-by target met, uptime, tokens used and server peaks. From **⋯ More → 📆 Review** or from **Project settings → Service**, open it.
- **Monthly token cap:** in **Project settings → Service**, a monthly limit of tokens set you can. At 80%, the daily brief warns you; at 100%, background runs for that project wait until next month or until the cap you raise. Still works, your own Wake does.
- **Good habits:** the service details first fill in, the web address correct keep, at the status dot daily look, every major incident write up, after each retro the improvements list check, and while fresh the month is, the monthly review read.

- **Groups:** you and two or more agents, from any project. Each member once to reply, each message you write wakes, so more tokens a big group uses.
